prompt:
I need the front end for Ledgerline. Correspondence software for research groups that ties messages with sponsored-programs accountants, PIs and vendors to the grants and charges they're about.

Who's using it: Teodora Ilic, lab and finance manager at a university coastal marine field station. She supports three faculty PIs and about 20 grad students and is the station's only point of contact with the central grants office.

What they're doing right now: The grants accountant flagged a $4,312 boat-fuel charge on a federal ocean-science grant as possibly unallowable and wants an explanation within 5 business days. Teodora is reading back through the thread and the related messages with the PI, Dr. Amaral, who is at sea with spotty email until Friday. She needs to write a reply that justifies the charge, ask the PI to confirm the cruise dates, and loop in the fuel vendor for an itemized invoice. She knows answers may take days to come back.

What's in the system at this point: Grant OCE-2291 'Kelp forest recovery after marine heatwaves', $1.2M over 3 years, year 2 of 3, $318,400 remaining. Flagged charge: Pacific Marine Fuel invoice #PMF-88213, $4,312.60, Oct 9, posted to account 'Field supplies' instead of 'Vessel operations'. Thread with accountant Greg Tanaka: 4 messages since Nov 10, latest Nov 13, response due Nov 20. Separate thread with Dr. Amaral: last reply Nov 8 from the R/V Sea Lark via satellite email. 2 other open threads: a $1,150 equipment return credit from a vendor, and a grad student reimbursement for $286 in dive-gear rental. Attachments: cruise plan PDF, vessel log excerpt Oct 7–11.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
